submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole is a retrospective detector of an INDEFINITE OR COMPARED AMOUNT, and its dominant job is the predicate of an expletive presentational clause: it is strongest (1.6-2.6, 62-100% of max) on the copula or light verb that follows expletive 'there'/'here' - 'there is/are/was/were/be/been/'s', 'there seems/appears/remains to be', 'here is/are' - and it holds most of that level for one or two more tokens into the indefinite NP ('there is little evidence', 'there is no doubt', 'there is a good chance', 'there are several ways'); every one of its 83 firings above 43% of max on a copula is that existential predicate (82 immediately after 'there'/'here', the 83rd the 'been' of 'there appears to have been'). Its weaker frame-free form (0.65-1.4, 25-55% of max) sits on the amount or comparison word itself - bare numerals and amount words ('two', 'three', 'seven', 'eight', 'a dozen', 'tons of', 'many', 'few', 'several', 'no', 'other', 'a lot of', 'much'/'little' before a noun) and the 'than' of the quantitative comparatives 'more than' (1.1) and 'other than' (1.4) - while it stays at 0-0.4 on copulas with definite or third-person subjects ('they are', 'it is', 'that is', 'the bridge is', 'he is'), on locative 'there'/'here' ('over there', 'the grass grows tall over there'), on definite totality and partitives ('all', 'each', 'every', 'both', 'most', 'some of', 'a number of', 'a kind of'), on bare comparative-adjective 'than' ('longer than', 'older than', 'steeper than', all <=0.65) and on 'more' outside the frame ('We need more volunteers', 0.05), on non-amount prepositions and particles ('in', 'on', 'at', 'across', 'along', 'past', 'over', 'beyond'), on ordinary nouns, verbs and adjectives, and on non-English text ('hay muchos', 'es gibt viele', 'il y a beaucoup' each read 0-0.07 after their opening token). Three leftovers it does not predict, each at 25-80% of max: the plural first-person and demonstrative copulas 'we are'/'those are'/'these are' (0.77-0.88), a few lexicalized chunks ('of course' 0.90, 'take place' 1.02, 'make sure' 0.91, 'take down' 2.09, 'bring up' 1.75, 'look up' 1.56), and a text's opening token, which reads 0.43-0.79 across the whole vocabulary (mean 0.59) whatever the token is.

rival_explanations: The pole is only an expletive-existential construction detector ('there'/'here' + copula), and its firings on bare numerals, 'many/few/several/no/other', 'more than' and the idiomatic chunks are a token-level tail that will not generalize, so 'I saw three bridges from the train window' and 'The museum sold more than two thousand tickets' should both be at baseline.

The pole is a general gradability/degree feature, so it should fire as strongly on ordinary comparative adjectives and intensifiers ('The bridge is longer than the old one', 'much colder', 'very clear') and on the definite totality words 'all/each/every/both/most' as it does on numerals and on 'more than'.

The pole is a fixed-multiword-chunk detector rather than a quantity feature: it fires on the second element of memorized phrases ('there is', 'more than', 'a lot of', 'of course', 'take down', 'make sure') regardless of meaning, so it should fire on other idioms such as 'as well as', 'in order to' and 'by means of', and should be indifferent to numerals that appear in novel phrasings.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bridge is older than the chapel on the hill, so we walked there after lunch.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Copula with a definite subject ('the bridge is') plus a bare comparative-adjective 'than' and locative 'there', all named 0-0.4 baseline cases under the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The sheep graze on the slope over there beyond the fence.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Locative 'there' with a named non-amount preposition 'beyond' and no copula, so the hypothesis predicts silence unlike its expletive-presentational frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The keys are here on the table, so please lock up when you leave.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'here' as a locative adverb after a definite-subject copula ('the keys are'), the mirror image of the claimed strong 'here is/are', predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: There I was, standing in the rain, and nobody drove past for an hour.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Fronted locative 'there' whose copula takes a definite pronoun subject, with 'past' a named non-amount preposition; the hypothesis restricts expletive 'there' to the presentational indefinite frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: By noon on Tuesday all the students had finished the exam.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Definite totality 'all', explicitly listed as a 0-0.4 case, in an ordinary narrative with no existential frame or amount word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: By Friday night most of the village had lost power in the storm.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Partitive totality 'most of', named baseline, with ordinary nouns and verbs and no presentational clause.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The wind felt much colder once the sun dropped behind the ridge.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'much' before an adjective rather than before a noun, the condition the hypothesis attaches to its weak amount firing, so it predicts silence on the intensifier.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The road up the valley is steeper than it looks from the village.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Bare comparative-adjective 'than' of the kind the hypothesis puts at <=0.65, with a definite-subject copula and the non-amount preposition 'from'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We need more volunteers for the food bank this winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'more' outside the 'more than' frame, which the hypothesis measured at 0.05, so it must stay at baseline despite the token being a claimed trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The museum catalogue lists each painting and the name of its owner.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same museum topic as a top example but with definite totality 'each' and no existential or amount, so the hypothesis predicts baseline on matching vocabulary alone.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Hay muchos libros antiguos en la biblioteca de la universidad.
